resource.name: PM Pitfalls Self-Audit
resource.description: Twenty corpus-derived PM pitfalls. User rates each, gets back the three highest-leverage to fix this quarter with personalized narration.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_score
tools.description: Deterministic. Returns the user's score (0-20) and the three highest-leverage pitfall IDs given their twenty answers.

answers.description: Twenty answers in pitfall-ID order (1 through 20).

exemplar_quotes.description: Pre-written corpus-anchored exemplar quote per top-three pitfall.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_narrate
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Takes the score and top three picks and returns personalized one-paragraph diagnoses + behavior suggestions per pitfall. Uses local corpus chunks for grounding.

user_context.description: Optional. User's role, stage, company size — sharpens the narration. Empty string if not provided.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_drift
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Returns the user's calibration drift if they've audited before — what shifted, what didn't, and a one-line read. Stores audit answers locally across runs.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web/URL-trick versions don't expose this tool. State requires the MCP App; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #44 PM Pitfalls Self-Audit. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.
dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Confirm enum-in-array works in MCP tool inputSchema.
Decide how pm_pitfalls_drift signals statefulness to the host.
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: Yes. MCP tool inputSchema follows JSON Schema (draft 7 subset). Enum constraints on array items are fully supported. The 'answers' field as specified is valid.

Use the tool-level annotations.readOnlyHint: false hint (now set above). The MCP Apps spec leaves consent UX to host discretion — there is no manifest-level requires-consent or data-retention flag. The host's confirmation UI handles per-call or install-time consent however that host chooses. Document persisted data in the tool description (answers array + timestamp per run) so the host's confirmation can convey it.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
